newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. balloonist pleased with solo trip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. balloonist pleased with solo trip.

text.p: U.S. adventurer Steve Fossett said on Monday he was tired but satisfied after landing his air balloon in northern India, halfway around the world from his U.S. starting point and short of his goal.

"It was a very good trip," Fossett told Reuters by telephone from Peeparpur village, some 550 km (330 miles) southeast of Delhi. "I wish I could have made the biggest achievement and flown around the world. But this is also successful."

In his first interview since landing in Nonkhar village at 0735 GMT on Monday, Fossett said he was pleased he broke two records during his six-day flight -- the longest distance covered by a balloon and the longest time spent in the air.

He said he landed safely in a field and was not injured, but his balloon ripped when it snagged in a tree. "It was a safe but rough landing," he said, adding that the wind was blowing at 24 km (15 miles) an hour. "It probably ruined the balloon."

Asked if he was disappointed he did not achieve his goal of encircling the globe, Fossett said: "Not really. This was also successful. It showed we are very close to being able to fly around the world."

Fossett, who said he had miscalculated the amount of fuel needed and did not get enough sleep, was asked when he might make a fresh bid to fly around the world nonstop. "I haven't had a chance to think of that," he said. "I just have to reflect."
